title_en: Xupu County Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital v. Xupu County Post and Telecommunications Bureau — dispute over failure to perform statutory duties

full_text_en:
Xupu County Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital v. Xupu County Post and Telecommunications Bureau — dispute over non-performance of statutory duties

Plaintiff: Xupu County Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital, Hunan Province.
Legal Representative: Li Qijun, President.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Ping, Director of Qiaojiang Judicial Office of Xupu County Judicial Bureau.

Defendant: Xupu County Post and Telecommunications Bureau, Hunan Province.
Legal Representative: He Jiliang, Director.
Agent ad litem: Li Qihong, Officer of Xupu County Post and Telecommunications Bureau.
Agent ad litem: Zhang Qi, Attorney at Hezhou Law Firm of Hunan Province.

The plaintiff, Xupu County Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital (hereinafter referred to as the County TCM Hospital), filed an administrative lawsuit before the Xupu County People's Court of Hunan Province, alleging that the defendant, Xupu County Post and Telecommunications Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the County PTB), failed to perform its duty to activate the "120" emergency hotline (hereinafter referred to as the "120" emergency hotline).

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff applied to the defendant for the activation of the "120" emergency hotline in accordance with the provisions of superior documents and approval from the competent authority. The defendant refused to act, causing the emergency vehicles and other facilities purchased by the plaintiff to remain inoperative to date, resulting in heavy losses. The plaintiff requested a ruling ordering the defendant to immediately perform its duty to activate the "120" emergency hotline and to compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 80,000.

Defendant's Defense: According to the Notice on Regulating the Management of "120" Medical Emergency Special Telephone Lines in the Province (Document No. 15) jointly issued by the Hunan Provincial Health Department and the Provincial Post and Telecommunications Bureau, the post and telecommunications authorities and the health administrative departments have the authority to determine the activation of the "120" emergency hotline. The plaintiff's application for the "120" emergency hotline did not comply with the provisions of Document No. 15. The "120" emergency hotline belongs to the entire society, not to the plaintiff. Pursuant to Document No. 15, the defendant is obliged to activate the "120" emergency hotline for Xupu County, but not for a specific hospital. In fact, the defendant has already activated the "120" emergency hotline for Xupu County, so there is no issue of non-performance of duty. The Post and Telecommunications Bureau is a public utility enterprise, not an administrative organ, and does not qualify as a defendant in an administrative lawsuit. Nor has it been authorized by any regulation to exercise administrative powers. The defendant has not made any specific administrative act against the plaintiff, so the plaintiff has no basis for filing an administrative lawsuit. If the plaintiff believes that the specific administrative act was made by the Hunan Provincial Post and Telecommunications Bureau through delegation, then the defendant in this case should be the Hunan Provincial Post and Telecommunications Bureau, not the Xupu County Post and Telecommunications Bureau. The plaintiff's claims do not comply with the provisions of the Administrative Procedure Law and should be dismissed by the court.

Facts Found by the Court:

Upon trial, the Xupu County People's Court found the following:

Document No. 15 prescribes the procedure for a medical institution applying to establish an emergency center and activate the "120" emergency hotline: after being designated by the local health administrative department and submitting a written report, and after being reviewed and approved by the prefecture or municipal health administrative department, the institution shall go through the activation procedures for the "120" emergency hotline with the local post and telecommunications department.

On August 15, 1997, the Hunan Provincial Health Department confirmed that the plaintiff, the County TCM Hospital, was a Grade II Level A general hospital with relatively comprehensive functions and an emergency department that had met the required standards, thus meeting the conditions for establishing an emergency center. On December 8 of the same year, the Xupu County Health Bureau designated the County TCM Hospital to establish an emergency center and activate the "120" emergency hotline. On the same day, the County TCM Hospital submitted to the defendant, the County PTB, the *Report on the Activation of the "120" Emergency Special Telephone Line*, which was approved by the County Chief and the Deputy County Chief in charge. On December 13, the County PTB installed the "120" emergency hotline for the County TCM Hospital and noted on the *Work Order for Installation, Removal, Relocation, Replacement of Telephones and Name Change/Transfer within the City* that the installation would be completed by December 16 and that the installation labor and material costs would be charged according to account number 3323208. However, this telephone line was never activated.

On July 20, 1998, the County PTB activated the "120" emergency hotline for the Xupu County People's Hospital, which had not been designated or approved by the health administrative department. On July 24, the County TCM Hospital submitted a *Report on Requesting the Establishment of the "120" Medical Emergency Special Telephone Line* to the Huaihua Municipal Health Bureau. On July 25, this report was approved by the Municipal Health Bureau. On July 27, the County TCM Hospital again made a written request to the County PTB to activate the "120" emergency hotline, but the County PTB still refused to do so.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including Document No. 15, the reports of the County TCM Hospital, documents from the Hunan Provincial Health Department, the Xupu County Health Bureau, and the Huaihua Municipal Health Bureau, as well as the *Work Order for Installation, Removal, Relocation, Replacement of Telephones and Name Change/Transfer within the City* from the County PTB. The above evidence was all cross-examined in court and found to be true, sufficient, and reliable.

Judgment of the First Instance:

The Xupu County People's Court held that the defendant, the County PTB, being an enterprise entity, does not have administrative functions for communications management and is not legally obligated to activate the "120" emergency hotline for the plaintiff, the County TCM Hospital. The plaintiff's claims could not be sustained. Accordingly, on September 9, 1998, the Xupu County People's Court rendered the following judgment:

The plaintiff's claims were dismissed.
Court costs of RMB 1,700 were to be borne by the County TCM Hospital.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, the County TCM Hospital appealed, contending that the County PTB bore an administrative duty regarding the activation of the "120" emergency hotline, and that the appellant's claims were well-founded and procedurally lawful. The appellant requested that the second-instance court set aside the original judgment, order the appellee, the County PTB, to perform its duty of activating the "120" emergency hotline for the County TCM Hospital, compensate the County TCM Hospital for losses caused by the non-activation of the "120" emergency hotline, and bear the litigation costs of this case.

Reasoning of the Huaihua Intermediate People's Court:

Upon trial, the Huaihua Intermediate People's Court held as follows:

For a long time, China has adopted a management model of integrating government administration with enterprise operations for the post and telecommunications departments. The post and telecommunications departments have both the authority of the administrative competent authority for post and telecommunications and participate in the market operations of the post and telecommunications sector. Through reform, although the postal service and telecommunications have been initially separated and some telecommunications departments have gradually become enterprise legal persons, due to the special characteristics of the telecommunications industry, the telecommunications market in China has not been fully liberalized. State-owned telecommunications enterprises remain the sole players in the wired communication market. The state's administrative management over the telecommunications sector is still implemented through these state-owned telecommunications enterprises. When these state-owned telecommunications enterprises exercise administrative management powers in continuation of past practices, they shall be regarded as "organizations authorized by laws and regulations" as referred to in Article 25, paragraph 4 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC.

The establishment of a "120" emergency center is a public welfare undertaking for medical institutions to save lives and heal the wounded. Considering that this undertaking can bring certain benefits to medical institutions, in order to ensure clear responsibility, maximize benefits and minimize drawbacks, and prevent delays in rescuing patients due to confusion, the government implements administrative management over the "120" emergency undertaking, stipulating that only one medical institution is allowed to establish a "120" emergency center and activate the "120" emergency hotline within one administrative region. The "120" emergency hotline is not an ordinary telephone that can be installed simply by paying the installation fee. Therefore, Document No. 15 jointly issued by the Provincial Health Department and the Provincial Post and Telecommunications Bureau provides that only a general hospital with relatively comprehensive functions, a high level of medical emergency capability, and an emergency department that meets the required standards can obtain the franchise to activate the "120" emergency hotline, after being designated by the county health bureau and reported to the prefectural or municipal health administrative department for approval. The joint document also provides that the post and telecommunications department shall charge only the telephone installation fee for activating the "120" emergency hotline, install the display system and computer auto-answer system free of charge, and waive the telephone usage charges. These preferential policies, which are markedly different from profit-making activities of enterprises, reflect both the government's administrative will to support this public welfare undertaking and the government's intention to uniformly regulate and manage this undertaking.

The fact that Document No. 15 was issued to the health administrative departments and post and telecommunications bureaus at the prefectural/municipal and county levels precisely demonstrates that the government intends to exercise administrative management over the activation of the "120" emergency hotline through these functional departments. The relationship between the post and telecommunications bureau and the medical institution being reviewed when implementing this document is not an equal civil relationship but a special administrative management relationship. The litigation arising from disputes between them is not a civil lawsuit but an administrative lawsuit. Although the defendant in an administrative lawsuit is usually an administrative organ, in order to protect the lawful rights and interests of the counterparty in administrative management and to supervise the lawful exercise of administrative powers by organizations authorized by laws and regulations, listing such organizations as defendants in administrative lawsuits and applying the Administrative Procedure Law to resolve administrative disputes between them and the counterparty in administrative management is conducive to resolving social conflicts and maintaining social stability.

According to the division of responsibilities under Document No. 15, the health administrative department is responsible for determining which medical institution is qualified to establish a "120" emergency center; the post and telecommunications bureau is responsible for reviewing whether the medical institution applying for activation of the "120" emergency hotline complies with the provisions of Document No. 15 and deciding whether to activate the "120" emergency hotline for it. The appellant, the County TCM Hospital, is a qualified unit approved to establish a "120" emergency center. After the County TCM Hospital submitted its application for activation of the "120" emergency hotline to the appellee, the County PTB, the County PTB proceeded with the installation. Later, the County PTB refused to perform its duty of activation for the County TCM Hospital on the ground that the activation of the "120" emergency hotline should be jointly determined by the post and telecommunications and health administrative departments. However, it privately activated the "120" emergency hotline for another hospital that had not been approved. This fact demonstrates that the so-called "should be jointly determined by the post and telecommunications and health administrative departments" was merely a misinterpretation of Document No. 15 by the County PTB in an attempt to share the power of determining activation with the health administrative department. When its attempt to share power failed, it no longer insisted on the claim of joint determination and unilaterally exercised the power to activate the "120" emergency hotline.

In summary, the appellee, the County PTB, refused to activate the "120" emergency hotline after receiving the application from the appellant, the County TCM Hospital. This constitutes an erroneous administrative act of non-performance of duties and should be corrected. The County PTB's defenses, including that the County TCM Hospital's application did not comply with the document provisions, that it had already performed its duty to activate the "120" emergency hotline, and that it lacked the qualification of a defendant in an administrative lawsuit, are all untenable and intended to evade responsibility. The appellant's main grounds for appeal are valid and should be sustained. Regarding the County TCM Hospital's claim for compensation for losses arising from the inability to operate the purchased emergency vehicles and other facilities normally, given that the emergency vehicles and equipment were not put into emergency use, this loss cannot be calculated as "direct losses" under Article 28(7) of the State Compensation Law of the PRC and therefore cannot be supported according to law. The first-instance court correctly found the facts but erred in applying the law, and the judgment should be amended accordingly. Therefore, pursuant to Article 54(3) of the Administrative Procedure Law, the Huaihua Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on October 28, 1998:

1. The administrative judgment of the Xupu County People's Court (1998) Xing Chu Zi No. 66 is set aside.
2. The appellee, Xupu County Post and Telecommunications Bureau, is ordered to perform its statutory duty within 15 days from the day following receipt of this judgment for the appellant, Xupu County Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital.

The litigation costs for the first and second instances, totaling RMB 3,400, shall be borne by the appellee, Xupu County Post and Telecommunications Bureau.
